testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A device that warns when air pressure is low.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that warns when air pressure is low.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure falls between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings must not be loose or covered with oil or grease. They must also not be too thin.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should turn on automatically when air tank pressure falls between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by blocking the wheels and releasing air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve will pop out and spring brakes will engage.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should move no more than:
questions.explanation: Check slack adjusters on level ground with wheels blocked and parking brake off. Pull each slack adjuster to make sure it moves no more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Always shift into a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you travel downhill.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Help prevent your wheels from locking up.
Stop your vehicle from speeding up when going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when the driver brakes hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: The air compressor connects to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine using gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. This happens when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage rate during an applied leakage test is ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What shows you how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before driving, check each slack adjuster. Park the vehicle, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters to check they move no more than about one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: What prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up when the brakes are applied.

questions.question: When spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of the springs and air pressure could damage the brakes.

questions.question: If air pressure drops between ____, a low pressure warning signal should already be on.
questions.explanation: A low pressure warning signal should turn on before air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi. The signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: How far does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under ideal conditions?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake when your brakes are hot from coming down a steep hill. Let the brakes cool first to avoid damage.

questions.question: The ____ between the air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is required between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is parked on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake because it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. Do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only when needed to help engine braking.

questions.question: When brakes get too hot, what can happen?

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.
The brakes will not work evenly.

questions.explanation: Brakes can overheat and lose their ability to slow the vehicle. Do not rely only on brakes. Use engine braking to help control your speed and prevent brake fade.

questions.question: What allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: If ABS is on only one axle, what happens?

options.text: You still have better control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have better control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only one part of the vehicle, you still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.
